messages:
Maria: heads-up, canary A/B is showing a p95 regression after the recent runtime merge. Long-seq (≈2048) requests up ~12% p95. CI perf job failed too.
CI-bot: perf-ci/job-542: regression detected — p95 +12% vs baseline (threshold +5%). logs: https://ci.internal/perf/job/542
Ajay: ugh. anybody see an obvious kernel or batching change in that merge?
Liam: bisect points to commit 7f2a3c8 from PR #1402. It touched threadpool scheduling + kernel auto-tune. Main tweak: allow_oversubscribe=true added to CPU kernel selection path.
Sophia: that could do it. Allowing oversubscribe can cause more thread contention under high concurrent load and push tail latency up.
Maria: confirmed reproducer with perf harness locally. Repro command: ```
PYTHONPATH=. pytest tests/perf/test_long_sequences.py::test_p95_baseline -k 2048 --runs 10
```
Liam: quick flamegraph diff (top few lines):
```
- runtime::kernel_dispatch (20% -> 28%)
- threadpool::worker_queue_wait (5% -> 13%)
- kv_cache::lookup (unchanged)
```
Ajay: so more time in dispatch + wait on the threadpool. smells like scheduling overhead rather than model compute.
Sophia: hypothesis: the batching heuristic timer was tightened in the same PR so batches are smaller, then oversubscribe changes scheduling fairness => context switches and higher p95.
Maria: CI traces show canary traffic had many small batches during a traffic spike. Ops controller currently at 10%->90% split.
Ops-bot: canary controller: split enforced, monitoring p95 over a 15m window.
Maria: proposal: add an automatic canary guard to pause rollouts when p95 > baseline by 5% for 3 consecutive 5m windows OR if perf CI fails. Should pause and page oncall.
Liam: agree. Also propose an auto-bisect job that runs a narrow perf harness across candidate commits to speed up culprit identification.
Ajay: quick mitigation: revert the allow_oversubscribe flag in the runtime image used by canary. I can build a revert image and stage it.
Deploy-bot: rollout change requested: update canary image -> runtime:sha-revert-1402 (staging).
CI-bot: note: perf-ci has a microbench but it only runs ~30s. we should add a p95 guard there so PRs like #1402 get rejected earlier.
Sophia: and we lack request-level telemetry for batch size distribution and threadpool queue depth per request. adding those metrics would speed debugging.
Maria: action items:
- Ajay: build+push revert image and apply to canary (ETA ~30m)
- Liam: implement rollout guard rule in controller (ETA ~2h)
- Sophia: add batch-size & worker-queue metrics to runtime (ETA EOD)
- Ops team: validate manual rollback flow if autopause triggers
Ajay: revert image built: gcr.internal/redwood/runtime:revert-1402-213456. Applying to canary now.
Deploy-bot: canary update started — routing 10% traffic to revert-1402-213456
Maria: monitoring p95 on revert slice, numbers look better after ~4 minutes, trending back to baseline.
CI-bot: perf-ci/job-542 re-run queued on revert image.
CI-bot: perf-ci/job-542: PASS — p95 within threshold.
Maria: great. Liam, once the guard lands we'll get automatic pauses next time.
Ajay: PR to revert main branch opened: https://git.internal/r/ajay/revert-1402-PR — includes tests and perf notes.
Sophia: long-term: we still want kernel auto-tune but need to retune heuristics (batch timer vs oversubscribe) for long sequences under concurrency.
Liam: plan: run a matrix sweep next week (batch_timer × oversubscribe × threadpool_size) against realistic load generator to find robust defaults.
Maria: thanks team. marking thread for follow-up once guard + metrics are in. :thumbsup:
